trigger_condition: CLI prints the anchor with empty parens, e.g. '(...)' capturing an empty string
potential_consequence: Notice/subtitle shows a blank reason instead of the intended fallback text, since '' ?? fallback stays ''

trigger_condition: Both authTimeout and ollamaDown anchors are simultaneously visible on the captured screen
guard_snippet: pick the match with the larger line index (most recent) instead of first FAILURES entry
potential_consequence: A later, real ollamaDown failure is masked by a stale earlier authTimeout anchor still on screen

trigger_condition: Terminal wraps mid-phrase and splits the anchor text itself (not just the trailing reason) across two lines
guard_snippet: match a wrap-tolerant anchor (e.g. join adjacent lines before includes check)
potential_consequence: detectFailure returns null, so the flow-stopping warning silently never surfaces the notice

trigger_condition: start() is called again (e.g. 'Try again' or a manual restart) after a previous run submitted values
guard_snippet: answeredValues.clear(); alongside occurrenceCounts.clear() in run()'s reset block
potential_consequence: getAnsweredValues() returns stale values from the aborted run mixed with the new one, once EPMCDME-14656 consumes it

trigger_condition: startSetup rejects with a non-object or message-less value (e.g. thrown null/plain Error without .raw)
potential_consequence: handleReject throws reading err.message, leaving the run's rows stuck without ever reaching settleInstallRow()

trigger_condition: A future FAILURES entry represents another non-fatal, flow-continuing warning besides authTimeout
potential_consequence: New warning-class failures never get proactive detection; the run appears to hang until it eventually errors elsewhere

trigger_condition: User dismisses/closes the proactive authTimeout notice, then the run later fails for a different reason via handleReject
guard_snippet: reset noticeFailureShown when the user closes without choosing Try again, or key the latch per failure id
potential_consequence: The real terminal failure never shows a notice at all once one has already been shown this run

trigger_condition: cancelSetup() races a run that settles successfully just before requestCancel() fires
guard_snippet: have cancelSetup report whether its own reject actually applied (check err.cancelled after await) rather than always returning true
potential_consequence: Caller believes it cancelled the run and restarts setup even though the prior run had just completed successfully

trigger_condition: CLI re-asks a prompt that carries no default hint (DEFAULT_HINT never matches)
guard_snippet: fall back to a longer idle/redraw-count heuristic when a prompt has no default hint
potential_consequence: The re-ask is indistinguishable from a cosmetic repaint and is swallowed forever, hanging the run (documented residual limit, still unhandled)
